1	---
2	title: "Tools: framing and vertical"
3	description: The agent tools that frame one clip on the canvas, switch camera layouts and make a tall or square version of a project, with every argument, answer and refusal.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These three tools fit pictures to a canvas: `reframe_clip` frames one clip, `switch_layout` arranges a camera and a screen, and `make_vertical_version` makes a 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1 version of the whole timeline.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…']}
12	  tools={['reframe_clip', 'switch_layout', 'make_vertical_version']}
13	  needs="Nothing to set up. Faces, people and salient regions are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
14	/>
15	
16	Times are in ticks, 600,000 a second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/) covers the `project` summary, the `new_clips` and `new_tracks` lists, and the sentence you get when a call changes nothing.
17	
18	## `reframe_clip`
19	
20	Frames one clip on the current canvas: following a subject, a recorded pointer or whoever is talking, or centring, fitting or rescaling it. **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** is this tool with `replace: true` on each selected clip and a **Backgrounds** track as `backdrop`, and **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** calls it for each clip. [Reframe a clip](/framing/reframe-clip/) explains the framing itself.
21	
22	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
23	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
24	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to frame. |
25	| `follow` | string | Yes | What to do: `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `cursor`, `layout`, `speaker`, `center`, `fit` or `keep`. Each has a section below. |
26	| `zoom` | number | No | How tight the frame is, 1 to 4 times the scale that fills the canvas. Default 1. |
27	| `where_empty` | string | No | What shows where there's nothing to follow: `fit`, the whole picture, or `center`. Default `fit`. |
28	| `backdrop` | integer | No | A track behind the clip's for a blurred copy of it. Left out, no copy is made. |
29	| `replace` | boolean | No | `true` removes the clip's own moves before framing. Default `false`, which composes the framing into them. |
30	| `from_width` | integer | No | `keep` and `layout` only: the width of the canvas the clip was placed on. Default the current canvas's. |
31	| `from_height` | integer | No | `keep` and `layout` only: the height of that canvas. Default the current canvas's. |
32	| `mics` | array of integers | With `speaker` | `speaker` only: two to four clip ids, the microphones of the people in the shot. |
33	| `mic_faces` | array of integers | No | `speaker` only: each microphone's face number, in `mics`' order. Left out, Frame Job matches them. |
34	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside that nest. Inside a nest the nest's canvas is the canvas. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
35	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by path. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
36	
37	Which kind reads which argument is in [Which options each kind reads](/framing/reframe-clip/#which-options-each-kind-reads). An argument a kind doesn't read is ignored, but `zoom` outside 1 to 4 stops the call whatever the kind.
38	
39	To frame for a new canvas, call `set_canvas` first and leave `rescale_clips` off, which is its default. `keep` and `layout` then take the old size in `from_width` and `from_height`.
40	
41	It answers `ok: true`, `cached` and the `project` summary. `cached` is false when an analysis ran first. A blurred copy adds its id to `new_clips`, and `new_tracks` when it needed a new track.
42	
43	The framing is written as the clip's position and scale and one action per move, as one undo step, **Reframe Clip**. A framing that would leave the clip exactly as it is changes nothing and makes no undo step.
44	
45	### `follow: subject`, `face`, `person` and `salient`
46	
47	These follow what Frame Job finds in the clip on your Mac. `subject` follows a face, else a person, else a salient region. `face`, `person` and `salient` follow only that kind.
48	
49	- The frame eases onto the subject and moves only when the subject leaves a dead zone.
50	- It cuts hard at each shot change.
51	- It holds a lost subject for 1 s, then follows another, or eases over 0.8 s to what `where_empty` says.
52	- It returns once a subject has been seen for 0.6 s.
53	- It frames two people together when both fit.
54	
55	The tool analyses the clip first. See [The analysis wait](#the-analysis-wait). A clip whose media has a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) can't use these four, because a recording with a cursor file follows its cursor, never faces. See [How a followed frame moves](/framing/reframe-clip/#how-a-followed-frame-moves).
56	
57	### `follow: cursor`
58	
59	Follows a screen recording's recorded pointer, read from its media's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). It reads the file at once, with no analysis and no wait.
60	
61	- The frame sits on the pointer and moves only when the pointer leaves a dead zone of 20 % of the frame's width and 12 % of its height.
62	- It arrives on each click outside that zone, in a move that ends on the click's frame.
63	- It holds still while the person types.
64	
65	The frame never shows the whole picture, so `where_empty` and `backdrop` do nothing here. A clip whose media has no cursor file can't use it. A cursor file that's missing or won't read stops the call, in a sentence naming it.
66	
67	### `follow: layout`
68	
69	Re-lays a camera clip's [camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/), and its screen's, on the current canvas. You can name the camera or the screen, and both are re-laid.
70	
71	Each switch made on `from_width` × `from_height` is recognised, to within 1 px and 0.001, and switched again here at the same time, length and curve.
72	
73	- **Side by Side** becomes **Stacked** on a canvas taller than wide.
74	- The cut pieces of the recording take the new layout.
75	- Any zoom on them is re-based so it shows the same part of the picture.
76	
77	It reads no `zoom`, `where_empty`, `backdrop` or `replace`, and it runs no analysis. A switch edited by hand can't be recognised, and the call stops, naming the clip and the action.
78	
79	### `follow: speaker`
80	
81	Frames a wide shot of two to four people on whoever is talking. Each person needs a microphone of their own, named in `mics`: a clip of a sound file or a camera's detached sound, each on its own track, and not the clip being framed. **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** offers this as Follow **Speaker**. See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/).
82	
83	- Who talks when is read from the microphones as [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) reads it at its default settings.
84	- Each microphone is matched to the face whose mouth moves with it, analysed on your Mac. Faces are numbered 1, 2 and so on from left to right.
85	- Each change of speaker is a hard cut, held at least 2 s.
86	- Two people talking at once are framed together when they fit, and otherwise the frame stays on the one already framed.
87	- While nobody talks, the last speaker stays.
88	
89	When the match is weak, with any pair agreeing under 0.2, the call stops and says where each face is, for example "face 1 at 28 % across the picture, face 2 at 71 %". Name each microphone's face in `mic_faces` and call again.
90	
91	A clip that changes shot can't be framed this way. Split it first with `split_at_shots`. `speaker` reads its microphones on what's open in the window, so a call addressed to a nest that isn't open stops and says to open it with `set_scope`.
92	
93	### `follow: center`
94	
95	Holds the frame on the middle of the picture for the whole clip, at `zoom`. It needs no analysis.
96	
97	### `follow: fit`
98	
99	Shows the whole picture for the whole clip, scaled to fit the canvas. It needs no analysis and doesn't read `zoom`. With `backdrop`, the blurred copy fills the canvas around it.
100	
101	### `follow: keep`
102	
103	Rescales the clip from the canvas it was made for, `from_width` × `from_height`, to the current one, as `set_canvas` does with `rescale_clips`. Every position and scale its actions set moves with it. With neither argument there's nothing to rescale.
104	
105	`keep` frames clips the other kinds won't, such as a title, a shape, a rotated clip or a clip on a matte track, as long as it has a picture. It reads no `zoom`, `where_empty`, `backdrop` or `replace`.
106	
107	### `zoom`, `where_empty`, `backdrop` and `replace`
108	
109	**`zoom`** sets how tight the frame is, from 1 to 4. At 1, the default, the picture covers the canvas with nothing to spare. `center`, the four following kinds, `cursor` and `speaker` read it, and `fit` and `keep` don't.
110	
111	**`where_empty`** is what the four following kinds and `speaker` show where there's nothing to follow: `fit`, the whole picture, or `center`, the middle of the picture.
112	
113	**`backdrop`** names a track for one blurred copy of the clip, for its whole length, made only when the framing shows the whole picture somewhere. That means `fit`, or a followed clip that falls back to `fit`.
114	
115	- The copy goes on the named track when that track is unlocked, isn't a matte and is free over the clip. Otherwise it goes on a new track at the back.
116	- It's the copy **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** makes.
117	- It keeps the clip's speed actions, so a ramped clip's copy shows the same frames.
118	
119	**`replace`** decides what happens to the actions the clip already has. By default they stay, and the framing is composed into the clip's position and scale and into every action end that moves or scales it, so a zoom or pan still happens inside the new framing.
120	
121	- The framing's own moves go in the gaps between the clip's actions. A move that would overlap one is shifted up to 0.5 s earlier, or else carried by that action, along its curve.
122	- A cut splits the action it lands in. A linear action plays as before and an eased one eases again on each side. A speed action, or one running past the clip's end, carries the cut instead.
123	- With `replace: true`, every `x`, `y` and `scale` is removed from the clip's action ends and the picture is fitted first. Volume and every other key stay, and an action left with nothing is removed.
124	
125	`keep` and `layout` don't read `replace`.
126	
127	### The analysis wait
128	
129	The four following kinds and `speaker` need the part of the file the clip plays analysed for shots, faces and subjects, with 1 s either side. The tool asks for what's missing and waits up to 60 s.
130	
131	Past that nothing changes. The answer is `ok: true` with `analyzing` and a `note`, so check for it rather than reading `ok` alone:
132	
133	| Key | What it holds |
134	| --- | --- |
135	| `analyzing.media` | The ids of the media still being analysed. |
136	| `analyzing.covered` | How much is done, from 0 to 1. |
137	| `note` | How far it got, and to call `reframe_clip` again. |
138	
139	The analysis carries on after the answer, so call again to apply the framing.
140	
141	- `center`, `fit`, `keep`, `layout` and `cursor` need no analysis.
142	- `speaker` also needs its microphones' loudness and speech, which Frame Job measures when a file is added. While that's still running the call stops and says to try again in a moment.
143	- If the analysis fails, the call stops, naming the analysis and the media.
144	- If the [Assistant](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) is stopped during the wait, nothing is framed.
145	- If the project or the open nest changes during the wait, nothing is framed. Call again.
146	
147	### Refusals
148	
149	A refused call changes nothing and answers one sentence. Frame Job first reads the values, and stops on an unknown clip, a `zoom` outside 1 to 4, a `from_width` or `from_height` of 0, an unknown `backdrop` track or, with `speaker`, an unknown clip in `mics`. Then it checks these in order:
150	
151	1. Anything but `keep` on a text, shape, graphic or adjustment clip.
152	2. A clip with no picture, or a crop or scale that leaves none.
153	3. A nest clip, then a still or image clip, with a following kind, `cursor` or `speaker`.
154	4. `cursor` on a clip whose media has no cursor file, then a following kind or `speaker` on one whose media has a cursor file.
155	5. Unless `keep` or `layout`: a clip on a matte track or cut by a matte, then a turned clip (a rotation, an action turning it, or a spin in its motion).
156	6. For `speaker`, its microphones:
157	   - `mics` doesn't hold two to four clips, or names a clip twice.
158	   - A microphone is the clip being framed, or has no sound from a media file.
159	   - A microphone's sound is off.
160	   - Two microphones are on one track.
161	   - `mic_faces` doesn't have one number for each microphone, names face 0, or names a face twice.
162	7. For `layout`:
163	   - The clip holds no camera layout.
164	   - A clip is laid out both as a camera and as a screen.
165	   - A screen layout has no camera switch in front of it.
166	   - The first switch isn't a layout Frame Job made on `from_width` × `from_height`, which means it was edited by hand.
167	
168	These need the analysis, the cursor file or the microphones, so they come last, in this order:
169	
170	8. For `speaker`:
171	   - A microphone is still being measured, or never speaks over the clip.
172	   - The clip changes shot.
173	   - Fewer faces show than there are microphones. A face counts when it's in at least a quarter of the clip's samples.
174	   - `mic_faces` names a face past the ones found.
175	   - Nobody speaks inside the clip.
176	   - The faces don't show who is whose.
177	9. With a copy to make: a nest clip, or a `backdrop` track that isn't behind the clip's.
178	10. A following kind with no analysis for the part that plays, or `cursor` with no recorded point in it.
179	
180	## `switch_layout`
181	
182	Lays out a camera clip and the screen recording behind it at a time, as [**Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸**](/framing/camera-layouts/) and the Picture sub-tab's [Layout section](/framing/layout-section/) do at the playhead. Those pages describe each layout and how far it reaches.
183	
184	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
185	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
186	| `camera` | integer | Yes | The camera clip's id: a clip with a picture playing at `at`. |
187	| `layout` | string | Yes | `corner`, `side_by_side`, `stacked`, `camera_full` or `screen_only`. |
188	| `at` | integer | Yes | When the switch starts, in ticks. Inside a nest, this is the nest's own time. |
189	| `screen` | integer | No | The screen clip's id, on a track behind the camera's. Left out, it's the clip playing at `at` on the front-most shown, non-matte track behind the camera's. With none there, the camera is laid out alone. |
190	| `shape` | string | No | `corner` only: `square`, `rounded` or `circle`. Default `square`. |
191	| `corner` | string | No | `corner` only: `bottom_right`, `bottom_left`, `top_right` or `top_left`. Default `bottom_right`. |
192	| `duration` | integer | No | How long the switch eases, in ticks. Default 0.5 s (300000). It's clamped to the clip and to its next layout action. |
193	| `curve` | string | No | How the switch eases: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. Default `ease_in_out`. |
194	| `through` | integer | No | Where the layout stops holding, in ticks, after `at`. |
195	| `focus` | array of 2 numbers, or null | No | `[x, y]`: the point of the camera's picture a crop is centred on, in the camera media's source pixels from the picture's centre, y down. It's clamped inside the picture. |
196	| `nest` | boolean | No | `true` nests a role's clips first when one of them zooms or moves after `at`, instead of stopping. Default `false`. |
197	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside that nest. Inside a nest the nest's canvas is the canvas. |
198	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by path. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
199	
200	| `layout` | The camera | The screen |
201	| --- | --- | --- |
202	| `corner` | In a corner box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third tall, 5 % in from the edges | At its full placement, where **Add Clip** puts it |
203	| `side_by_side` | Cropped to fill the right third | Fitted in the left two-thirds |
204	| `stacked` | Filling the rest below the screen | Across the top |
205	| `camera_full` | Fills the canvas | At its full placement |
206	| `screen_only` | Hidden where it is, at opacity 0 | At its full placement |
207	
208	Each role gets one layout action at `at`. At a clip's first frame the layout becomes its base, and a one-frame action marks the cut. A layout action already starting at `at` is replaced, and one still easing at `at` is shortened to end there.
209	
210	The layout holds. Every later clip on the camera's track, and on the screen's, that starts before the next switch on that track, `through` or the track's end takes it as its base and keeps its own actions.
211	
212	With `focus` left out or null, the tool fills it as the menu does, from the middle of the camera clip's person masks when they're cached for every frame it plays. Otherwise the crop is centred. A filled `focus` is dropped when `nest: true` nests the camera, but a `focus` you send goes as given.
213	
214	It answers `ok: true`, `focus` (the `[x, y]` sent, or null when none was) and the `project` summary, with `new_clips` and `new_tracks` when `nest: true` made a nest. It's one undo step, **Camera Layout**.
215	
216	A negative `at`, a `duration` that isn't positive, a `through` not after `at`, or a `focus` that isn't two numbers stops the call before anything else. Then it's refused, with nothing changed and the clip named, when:
217	
218	- the camera has no picture, or doesn't play at `at`, and the same for a `screen` you name
219	- `screen` isn't on a track behind the camera's
220	- `side_by_side` or `stacked` has no screen
221	- the camera is a nest clip and the shape is `rounded` or `circle`
222	- a clip in the layout's reach holds a zoom or another action that moves it after `at`. A screen still at its full placement isn't asked in `corner`, `camera_full` and `screen_only`, since its zooms keep playing. Send `nest: true` to nest that role's clips first, in the same step, so the layout moves the nest and the zoom stays inside it.
223	- with `nest: true`, one of the clips to nest is already laid out, or nesting would make the camera a nest clip in a `rounded` or `circle` corner
224	- the project or the open nest changes while the tool reads the person masks. Call again.
225	
226	## `make_vertical_version`
227	
228	Makes a vertical (9:16), 4:5 or square (1:1) version of the top-level timeline, as [**File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**](/framing/make-vertical-version/) does. [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/) goes through what happens to each kind of clip. The tool has no `scope`, because it only works on the top-level timeline.
229	
230	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
231	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
232	| `shape` | string | Yes | The new shape: `9:16`, `4:5` or `1:1`. |
233	| `follow` | string | No | What a movie clip follows: `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `speaker` or `center`. Default `subject`. |
234	| `zoom` | number | No | How tight, 1 to 4 times the scale that fills the new canvas. Default 1. |
235	| `where_empty` | string | No | What a followed clip shows where nothing is found: `fit`, the whole picture on a blurred copy, or `center`. Default `fit`. |
236	| `mics` | array of integers | With `speaker` | `speaker` only: two to four clip ids, each a clip of a sound file on its own track, standing for that track as one person's microphone. |
237	| `mic_faces` | array of integers | No | `speaker` only: each microphone's face number, in `mics`' order, faces numbered 1, 2 and so on from left to right. Left out, Frame Job matches them. |
238	| `copy` | boolean | No | `true` opens the version as a new project. `false` applies it to the project you name. Default `true`. |
239	| `path` | string | No | With `copy` only: where to save the new project, as an absolute path. `.framejob` is added when missing. Nothing may exist there yet. Without it the copy opens untitled. |
240	| `captions` | boolean | No | `true` re-pages each word caption track on the new canvas. `false` keeps caption tracks as placed, like any other clip. Default `true`. |
241	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by path. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
242	
243	The new canvas keeps the old short side, rounded down to even. From 1920 × 1080 that's 1080 × 1920, 1080 × 1350 or 1080 × 1080.
244	
245	It answers these keys beside `ok: true`:
246	
247	| Key | What it holds |
248	| --- | --- |
249	| `canvas` | The new `width` and `height`. |
250	| `cached` | False when an analysis ran first. |
251	| `clips` | One row per clip with a picture, in id order: `clip`, `treatment`, and `reason` when it did less than asked. |
252	| `cursor` | The clips followed by their cursor. |
253	| `speaker` | The clips framed on whoever is talking, each `clip`, `mics` and `mic_faces`. |
254	| `relaid` | Each re-laid switch, in time order: `camera`, `at` (ticks), `from`, `to` and, for a corner, `shape`. `from` and `to` are `switch_layout`'s layout words. |
255	| `backgrounds` | Whether the **Backgrounds** track was kept. |
256	| `more_tracks` | How many further tracks were made behind it, where clips overlap. |
257	| `re_eased` | How many actions were eased again at a cut. |
258	| `moves_carried` | How many actions carry a framing move. |
259	| `summary` | The same text the sheet shows, in sentences. |
260	| `captions` | `relaid` and `kept`, as `relay_captions` answers them. It's absent with `captions: false`. |
261	| `graphics` | `resized` (a count), `updated` (names) and `listed` (each `name` and `reason`). |
262	| `project` | The summary of the copy, or of the project you named. |
263	| `carried` | A copy only: the `files`, `bytes` and `seconds` carried over. |
264	| `saved` | With `path`: where the copy was saved. |
265	
266	A clip's `treatment` is one of:
267	
268	| `treatment` | What happened |
269	| --- | --- |
270	| `followed` | It follows its subject, cursor or speaker. |
271	| `whole` | It's shown whole on a blurred copy for its full length. |
272	| `kept` | It's kept as placed, rescaled from the old canvas. |
273	| `refilled` | A blurred copy or plate is made to fill the new canvas. |
274	| `removed` | A blurred copy was removed, because its clip is now followed. |
275	| `resized` | A graphic was re-sized to the new canvas. |
276	| `relaid` | A camera or screen was re-laid. |
277	| `not_followed` | It wasn't followed, and `reason` says why and what it did instead. |
278	
279	### Subject following
280	
281	Each movie clip that fills the old frame on one side is framed with `reframe_clip` from the old canvas, following `follow`, at `zoom` and `where_empty`. Where nothing is found, it's shown whole on a blurred copy by default. The copies go on a new **Backgrounds** track at the back, which is removed when nothing needs it.
282	
283	With `follow: center` the picture's centre is held and nothing is analysed.
284	
285	- A clip Frame Job won't frame, because it's on a matte track, rotated or spinning, is kept as placed, as `not_followed` with the reason.
286	- A movie whose file is missing is kept as placed in the same way, unless `follow` is `center`.
287	
288	### Screen recordings follow the cursor
289	
290	A screen recording whose media has a cursor file follows its cursor, never faces, with any `follow` but `center`, which centres it. Its own zooms and pans are replaced. If the cursor file can't be read it's shown whole on a blurred copy, and its `reason` says so.
291	
292	### `follow: speaker` in a vertical
293	
294	With `follow: speaker`, a movie clip of two to four people, playing beside two or more of the microphones in `mics`, is framed on whoever is talking, as [`follow: speaker`](#follow-speaker) frames it. Every other movie clip follows its faces.
295	
296	- Each clip in `mics` stands for its track. Under a shot, the clip used is the one on that track that overlaps the shot most.
297	- A clip on a microphone's track is never framed this way, and neither is a screen recording with a cursor file.
298	- Faces are matched by Frame Job, or named with `mic_faces`.
299	- When one clip can't be framed on the speaker, such as a clip that changes shot, it follows its faces instead and its `reason` says why. The rest of the call goes ahead.
300	
301	See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/).
302	
303	### Camera layouts re-laid
304	
305	A camera and the screen behind it laid out with **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸** are re-laid, not reframed, with [`follow: layout`](#follow-layout) once per camera. Each switch is solved again for the new canvas at its old time, length and curve, and **Side by Side** becomes **Stacked** on a tall canvas. They're never followed and get no blurred copy.
306	
307	Their `treatment` is `relaid`. A layout edited by hand is kept as placed, as `not_followed` with the reason. The answer's `relaid` lists each switch.
308	
309	### Stills, graphics, titles and plates
310	
311	| The clip | What happens | `treatment` |
312	| --- | --- | --- |
313	| A still picture or a nest that fills the frame on one side | Centred, with the reason | `not_followed` |
314	| A graphic exactly the old canvas's size | Re-sized to the new canvas. Its position and its action ends' positions move by the two sides' ratios, and its scale is kept. | `resized` |
315	| A title, a picture-in-picture, a shape or a graphic of another size | Kept as placed, rescaled from the old canvas | `kept` |
316	| An old **Blurred Background** copy | Removed when its clip is followed, else made to fill the new canvas | `removed` or `refilled` |
317	| A full-frame shape plate, or an image named **Background** | Made to fill the new canvas | `refilled` |
318	
319	### A copy or in place
320	
321	By default a new project opens, named `<name> (9:16)`, `(4:5)` or `(1:1)`, holding the change as its one undo step, **Make Vertical**. It carries the project's caches and analysis, and the project you named doesn't change. With `path`, the copy is saved there first. The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks before a call that names a `path`.
322	
323	With `copy: false`, the change goes into the project you named as one undo step, **Make Vertical**.
324	
325	### Captions re-paged
326	
327	Each word caption track is re-paged on the new canvas from its own words, as `relay_captions` does, and a track it can't re-lay is kept as placed. The answer's `captions` lists those `relaid` and those `kept`, each kept one with its reason. With `captions: false`, caption tracks stay as placed and the key is left out. See [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/).
328	
329	### Bundled templates updated
330	
331	In a copy, the project's own older copies of the bundled `lower-third`, `title-card`, `callout`, `bar-chart`, `counter` and `kinetic-type` templates are rewritten with the current template, which fits a tall canvas. A module is known by its text, never its name, and its old text is kept as its previous revision. The names land in `graphics.updated`.
332	
333	With `copy: false` nothing is rewritten, and each one is in `graphics.listed` with the reason. A module that sizes itself by the canvas's height is listed either way, because it may not fit the narrow frame.
334	
335	### Analysis and refusals
336	
337	The tool analyses the movie clips on your Mac first, as `reframe_clip` does, and waits up to 60 s. A screen recording with a cursor file isn't analysed, and neither is anything with `follow: center`. Past 60 s nothing is made. The answer is `ok: true` with `analyzing` and a `note`, as in [The analysis wait](#the-analysis-wait), so call again.
338	
339	It's refused, with nothing made, when:
340	
341	- a nest is open. Leave it with `set_scope` first.
342	- `path` is given with `copy: false`
343	- another open project holds `path`, or something already exists there
344	- the canvas already has that shape
345	- the canvas can't change or the **Backgrounds** track can't be added, such as when the project already has too many tracks
346	- a clip can't be framed even with `keep`
347	- `follow: speaker` has no `mics`, or a clip id in `mics` isn't a clip
348	- `follow: speaker` finds no movie clip playing beside two of the microphones
349	- a microphone is still being analysed or never speaks
350	- the analysis fails or is stopped, or the project or the open nest changes during the wait

27	| `video` | boolean | No | Sets each piece's picture on or off. Default: the clip's own setting. |
28	| `audio` | boolean | No | Sets each piece's sound on or off. Default: the clip's own setting. |
29	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside that nest, where the times and tracks are the nest's. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
30	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by path. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
31	
32	Each piece is exactly what two splits at its range's ends would leave in the middle: the same source frames at the same times, with speed, a ramp, reversal, a graphic's own timeline, timed words and actions cut as a split cuts them. So a piece of a synced camera shows that camera's own frame at every time. Pieces get new ids, no transition and no link.
33	
34	Each range's ends snap to the frame grid, a pair written backwards is the same range, and a range that's empty on the grid is skipped. Ranges may touch. If every range is empty, nothing changes.
35	
36	It answers `ok: true`, `new_clips` (the pieces) and the `project` summary. It's one undo step, **Copy Pieces**.
37	
38	An unknown clip or track stops the call, and so does an empty `ranges`. Then it's refused, with nothing changed, in this order:
39	
40	1. The clip is a nest clip, because a piece of it would replay the nest from its first frame.
41	2. A range is outside the clip.
42	3. Two ranges overlap.
43	4. The destination track is locked.
44	5. The destination track holds a clip over a range. The sentence names that clip and its ends.

46	## `switch_angle`
47	
48	Re-picks one shot from another camera, as [**Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸**](/multicam/switch-angle/) does.
49	
50	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
51	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
52	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The shot to re-pick: a clip on the program track. |
53	| `angle` | integer | Yes | The id of the track to re-pick it from. |
54	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by path. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
55	
56	An angle is a track whose video clips cover the shot's whole span. A clip with its picture off, or on a hidden track, still counts. The menu lists at most nine angles, and the tool can name any track.
57	
58	The shot is deleted and the angle copied over the same span, one piece per angle clip the span crosses, each with the shot's picture and sound settings. Where two angle clips overlap, the later one takes over at its own start. The clips either side are trimmed back to their old edges, so a dissolve on either edge is formed again with its kind, curve and sound shape.
59	
60	The shot's grade, punch-in, actions and other settings don't carry over.
61	
62	It takes no `scope`. It works in the nest `set_scope` has open.
63	
64	| Key | What it holds |
65	| --- | --- |
66	| `ok` | `true`. |
67	| `step` | **Switch Angle**, or **Switch Angle (transition removed)** when a dissolve couldn't be formed again against a short piece and was dropped. |
68	| `pieces` | The new clip ids, in time order. |
69	| `transitions_removed` | How many dissolves were dropped, from 0 to 2. |
70	| `project` | The summary. |
71	
72	It's one undo step, named as `step` says. An unknown clip or track stops the call. It's refused, with nothing changed, when:
73	
74	- the angle is the shot's own track
75	- the shot's track is locked
76	- the shot is linked to its detached sound
77	- the angle doesn't cover the shot. The sentence names the first tick with nothing to show.
78	- an edge is held short of where it needs to go, for example by a speed ramp. The sentence names the clip and the tick it reached.
79	- a step of the re-pick is refused, in that step's own sentence
80	
81	## `switch_by_speaker`
82	
83	Cuts a Program track from synced cameras, showing whoever talks on each microphone, as [**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) does. Run `sync_audio` first, because it trusts where the clips sit. Then select the clips with `set_selection`, because it reads the selected clips.
84	
85	It takes no `scope`. It works in the nest `set_scope` has open.
86	
87	### Switch by Speaker options
88	
89	Every argument is optional. [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/) explains the ones the sheet shows.
90	
91	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
92	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
93	| `speakers` | array of `{mic, angle}` | No | Who is who: one object per person, both track ids. A camera's detached sound may be a `mic`. One `mic` named for two or more cameras is [faces mode](#faces-mode). Default: the pairing the selection implies. |
94	| `wide` | integer or null | No | The camera shown when nobody or everybody talks, or null for none. It must be one of the cameras. Default: the one camera no speaker uses, when exactly one is left, and none in faces mode. |
95	| `from` | integer | No | The range's start, in ticks. Give it with `to`. |
96	| `to` | integer | No | The range's end, after `from`. Give it with `from`. |
97	| `min_shot` | number | No | Seconds. A shorter shot merges into a neighbour. 0.5 to 30. Default 2, or 3 in faces mode. |
98	| `min_turn` | number | No | Seconds. A shorter turn, such as a reply, starts no shot. 0.2 to 10. Default 1. The sheet doesn't show it. |
99	| `lead` | number | No | Seconds a cut comes before the new speaker's first word. 0 to 1. Default 0.2. |
100	| `crosstalk` | string | No | What a second or more of crosstalk shows: `wide`, or `hold` to stay on the current speaker. Default `wide`. |
101	| `bleed_db` | number | No | How many dB below a speaker's own level counts as the other person's voice bleeding in, never a turn. 3 to 40. Default 15. |
102	| `dominance_db` | number | No | How many dB one active microphone must lead every other to count alone. 0 to 30. Default 8. The sheet doesn't show it. |
103	| `wide_after` | number or null | No | Seconds. Once one person has held the screen this long, cut to the wide for `min_shot`. 2 to 600. Default null, which is off. |
104	| `mute_cameras` | boolean | No | Turns the cameras' own sound off inside the range. Default: on when no microphone is a camera. |
105	| `track` | integer | No | Replaces the shots on this track, an earlier Program track, instead of adding one. It must be unlocked, in front of the cameras, hold no selected clip, and hold only pieces of the cameras over the range. |
106	| `apply` | boolean | No | `false` answers without editing. See [Preview with `apply: false`](#preview-with-apply-false). Default `true`. |
107	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by path. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
108	
109	A number outside its range stops the call and says the range, where the sheet would pull it back in.
110	
111	### What it reads
112	
113	- **The cameras:** a camera is a track holding a selected clip with a picture.
114	- **The microphones:** by default these are the tracks holding a selected sound-only clip. With none, each camera with sound is its own microphone. Microphones are paired with cameras front to back, and a track you name in `speakers` still needs a selected clip with its sound on.
115	- **The range:** `from` and `to`, else the In–Out range, else the extent of the selected camera clips.
116	
117	It reads each microphone's loudness and speech, which Frame Job measures when a file is added. Then it cuts a shot `lead` before each new speaker's turn, holds through short replies and silence, shows the wide during crosstalk, and merges shots under `min_shot`.
118	
119	### What it writes
120	
121	It's one undo step, **Switch by Speaker**:
122	
123	- a new track named **Program** directly in front of the front-most camera, or with `track`, that track cleared over the range
124	- one [`copy_pieces`](#copy_pieces) for each camera clip a shot crosses, picture on and sound off
125	- the camera tracks hidden, or, when a camera track holds clips outside the range, its clips split at the range's ends with their pictures off inside
126	- with `mute_cameras`, the cameras' own sound off inside the range, never on a microphone's track
127	
128	Nothing outside the range changes, and the microphones are never edited. A selected clip that gets split keeps both halves selected.
129	
130	### What it answers
131	
132	| Key | What it holds |
133	| --- | --- |
134	| `ok` | `true`. |
135	| `applied` | Whether the project was edited. |
136	| `step` | **Switch by Speaker**. Only when applied. |
137	| `track` | The Program track's id. Null when not applied and no `track` was named. |
138	| `shots` | Each shot's `angle`, `start` and `end`. |
139	| `ops` | How many edits it makes. |
140	| `added` | How many clips it adds. |
141	| `speakers` | The pairing used, each `mic` and `angle`. |
142	| `wide` | The wide camera, or null. |
143	| `mute_cameras` | The value used. |
144	| `mode` | `microphones` or `faces`. |
145	| `note` | Faces mode only: "Faces guess who is talking; check the cuts." |
146	| `project` | The summary. |
147	
148	### Preview with `apply: false`
149	
150	Pass `apply: false` to see the planned shots without editing the project. The answer has the same keys, with `applied` false and no `step`. It's the same work as a real run, so it stops for the same reasons.
151	
152	### Faces mode
153	
154	When one microphone is shared by two or more cameras, their faces decide who talks. This is the default when the selection holds exactly one microphone, and you get it by naming one `mic` for two or more cameras. See [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/).
155	
156	While the microphone hears speech, each camera's on-device face analysis says whose mouth moves most, going by the largest face in the picture. A camera wins with 1.5 times the next camera's movement, and otherwise it counts as crosstalk.
157	
158	- A named `wide` takes no part in deciding who talks. Named without `speakers`, a speaker on it who shares a microphone is left out.
159	- `min_shot` defaults to 3.
160	- `mode` says `faces`, and `note` says the cuts are a guess, so check them.
161	
162	Where the sheet would show the Analyzing sheet, the tool finds the faces it still needs and waits up to 60 s. Past that it's refused, and what it covered is kept. Call it again to continue.
163	
164	### Switch by Speaker refusals
165	
166	Nothing changes when a call is refused. It stops first on a value it can't read, such as an unknown track, a `wide` that isn't a camera, only one of `from` and `to`, or a `to` not after `from`.
167	
168	These are checked together, and the sentence names every one that applies:
169	
170	- fewer than two cameras, or more than nine
171	- a speaker without a microphone or without a camera
172	- one microphone for two speakers, outside faces mode
173	- a microphone still being analysed, or with no speech in the range
174	- speech detection isn't available on this Mac
175	- a camera whose faces are still being found, or that shows no face whose mouth can be read
176	- a stretch no camera covers
177	
178	These each stop the call on their own:
179	
180	- a faces analysis that failed, was stopped, or didn't finish within the wait
181	- the project or the open nest changed during the wait
182	- more clips than the project may hold. Raise `min_shot` to make fewer shots.
183	- a `track` that can't take the shots: it's locked, it holds a selected clip, it isn't in front of the cameras, it has nothing in the range, or it holds a clip that isn't a piece of a camera
184	- a camera clip linked by **Detach Audio**. Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first.

3	/// `reframe_clip` (road map "creator-jobs" VR2a2 and VR2b1, spec §11 VR-26…VR-28):
4	/// the op tool whose `subjects` the app fills from the analysis cache. It mirrors
5	/// Clip ▸ Follow Subject… (VR2b2, spec §11 VR-29: this op with `replace: true` per
6	/// selected clip and a "Backgrounds" backdrop track); every refusal is the core's
7	/// sentence, and Swift copies none of VR-26's or VR-27's rules (`replace` is
8	/// passed through as the caller sent it). It reads no `UserDefaults` (AU-68 (f)).
9	///
10	/// **Runs on the SERVER thread** (`creatorOffMainTools`), in three hops:
11	/// - the first main hop resolves the arguments and TRIES the op with no
12	///   `subjects`, scoped, on the document's project without committing (as the
13	///   inspector's probe does). Only the core's "no subjects" refusal (VR-26's
14	///   tenth, LAST so every other one answers the trial) leads to the analysis;
15	///   an applied, identity or other refused trial goes straight to the last
16	///   hop;
17	/// - the wait is `split_at_shots`'s: a new lane owner and CJ-25's bound. Past
18	///   it the same requests are wanted again on that owner, held by
19	///   `FramingWant` until every one has ended or the document closes, and the
20	///   answer is `analyzing`, with no edit;
21	/// - the subjects are read off main (`FramingSubjects`), and the last main hop
22	///   refuses a changed project or scope, then applies one op as one undo step,
23	///   "Reframe Clip".
24	///
25	/// `follow: cursor` (VR5, spec §11 VR-50 (i)) never waits: after the trial's "no
26	/// subjects" the first hop finds the media's cursor file (`AutoZoom.cursorFiles`, its
27	/// sentences the refusal), and the file is opened and read off main
28	/// (`FramingCursor.read`) in place of the analysis; the answer's `cached` is true.
29	///
30	/// `follow: speaker` (VR6a, spec §11 VR-60 (c)) waits for the analysis as a following
31	/// kind does; its `mics` and `mic_faces` are passed through, a call addressed to a
32	/// container other than the open one is refused before the trial, and the last main
33	/// hop adds `turns` to the subjects (`FramingSpeaker.turns`, Switch by Speaker's reading
34	/// of the microphones, its refusals SW-24's).
35	extension AgentServer {
36	
37	    /// What the first main hop resolves.
38	    private struct FramingCall {
39	        let document: ProjectDocument
40	        let clip: UInt32
41	        let follow: FramingFollow
42	        let zoom: Double?
43	        let whereEmpty: FramingWhereEmpty?
44	        let fromWidth: UInt32?
45	        let fromHeight: UInt32?
46	        let backdrop: UInt32?
47	        let replace: Bool?
48	        let mics: [UInt32]?
49	        let micFaces: [UInt32]?
50	        /// The analysis to read, or nil when the trial needs none.
51	        let reading: FramingReading?
52	        /// The cursor file to read for `follow: cursor`, or nil.
53	        let cursor: CursorReading?
54	        let asked: ReelProject
55	        let scope: UInt32?
56	
57	        func op(subjects: [String: Any]?) -> ReelOp {
58	            .reframeClip(
59	                clip: clip, follow: follow, zoom: zoom, whereEmpty: whereEmpty,
60	                fromWidth: fromWidth, fromHeight: fromHeight, backdrop: backdrop,
61	                replace: replace, mics: mics, micFaces: micFaces, subjects: subjects)
62	        }
63	
64	        /// The same call reading `reading` or `cursor` instead.
65	        func with(reading: FramingReading?, cursor: CursorReading?) -> FramingCall {
66	            FramingCall(
67	                document: document, clip: clip, follow: follow, zoom: zoom,
68	                whereEmpty: whereEmpty, fromWidth: fromWidth, fromHeight: fromHeight,
69	                backdrop: backdrop, replace: replace, mics: mics, micFaces: micFaces,
70	                reading: reading, cursor: cursor, asked: asked, scope: scope)
71	        }
72	    }
73	
74	    /// The clip's media, its windows and its cursor file (VR-50 (i)).
75	    private struct CursorReading {
76	        let media: MediaSnapshot
77	        let windows: [ClosedRange<Ticks>]
78	        let files: [UInt32: URL]
79	    }
80	
81	    /// The clip's media, its windows, the cache folder and what is missing.
82	    private struct FramingReading {
83	        let media: MediaSnapshot
84	        let windows: [ClosedRange<Ticks>]
85	        let cacheDir: URL
86	        let requests: [AnalysisRequest]
87	    }
88	
89	    func reframeClip(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
90	        let stop = AgentLane.shared.callCancel  // the assistant's Stop (spec §11 AI-16)
91	        guard !Thread.isMainThread else {
92	            throw ToolError(
93	                message: "reframe_clip must run on the server thread — its name is missing "
94	                    + "from AgentServer.creatorOffMainTools.")
95	        }
96	        let call = try onMain { try self.resolveFraming(a) }
97	        var subjects: [String: Any]?
98	        if let reading = call.reading {
99	            if !reading.requests.isEmpty,
100	                let analyzing = try waitForAnalysis(
101	                    reading.requests, document: call.document, stop: stop,
102	                    unmade: "nothing was framed",
103	                    note: { percent in
104	                        "Still analyzing the media of clip \(call.clip) (\(percent) %); call "
105	                            + "reframe_clip again to apply."
106	                    })
107	            {
108	                return analyzing
109	            }
110	            subjects = FramingSubjects.read(
111	                media: reading.media, windows: reading.windows, cacheDir: reading.cacheDir)
112	        }
113	        if let cursor = call.cursor {
114	            do {
115	                guard let track = try AutoZoom.readTracks(cursor.files)[cursor.media.id] else {
116	                    throw ToolError(message: "Media \(cursor.media.id)'s cursor file was not read.")
117	                }
118	                subjects = try FramingCursor.read(
119	                    track, media: cursor.media, windows: cursor.windows)
120	            } catch let error as ToolError {
121	                throw error
122	            } catch {
123	                throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
124	            }
125	        }
126	        let cached = call.reading?.requests.isEmpty ?? true
127	        return try onMain {
128	            let document = call.document
129	            guard document.project === call.asked, document.scope == call.scope else {
130	                throw ToolError(
131	                    message: "the project changed while reframe_clip read the clip's analysis, "
132	                        + "so nothing was framed. Call reframe_clip again.")
133	            }
134	            // VR-60 (c): who speaks when, read on this hop from the microphones' caches.
135	            var filled = subjects
136	            if call.follow == .speaker, filled != nil,
137	                let shown = document.editedProject.snapshot.clip(call.clip)
138	            {
139	                do {
140	                    filled?["turns"] = try FramingSpeaker.turns(
141	                        document: document, clip: shown, mics: call.mics ?? [])
142	                } catch let refusal as FramingSpeaker.Refusal {
143	                    throw ToolError(message: "reframe_clip was refused: " + refusal.sentence)
144	                }
145	            }
146	            return try self.editResult(
147	                document, FramingWant.actionName, [call.op(subjects: filled)],
148	                ["cached": cached])
149	        }
150	    }
151	
152	    /// Every argument in the op's order, the trial, and — only when the core
153	    /// answered "no subjects" — what the analysis must cover.
154	    private func resolveFraming(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> FramingCall {
155	        let document = try target(a)
156	        _ = try idArg(a, "clip")
157	        let follow = try requiredEnumArg(a, "follow", FramingFollow.self)
158	        let clip = try clipArg(a, "clip", document)
159	        var backdrop: UInt32?
160	        if let raw = a["backdrop"], !(raw is NSNull) {
161	            backdrop = try trackArg(a, "backdrop", document).id
162	        }
163	        let call = FramingCall(
164	            document: document, clip: clip.id, follow: follow, zoom: try doubleArg(a, "zoom"),
165	            whereEmpty: try enumArg(a, "where_empty", FramingWhereEmpty.self),
166	            fromWidth: try sideArg(a, "from_width"), fromHeight: try sideArg(a, "from_height"),
167	            backdrop: backdrop, replace: try boolArg(a, "replace"),
168	            mics: try numbersArg(a, "mics"), micFaces: try numbersArg(a, "mic_faces"),
169	            reading: nil, cursor: nil, asked: document.project, scope: document.scope)
170	        let scope = effectiveScope(document)
171	        if follow == .speaker, scope != document.scope {
172	            throw ToolError(
173	                message: "reframe_clip was refused: follow speaker reads its microphones on the "
174	                    + "open timeline; open that nest first with set_scope")
175	        }

177	        do {
178	            trial = try document.project.applying(call.op(subjects: nil).scoped(scope))
179	        } catch {
180	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
181	        }
182	        guard case .refused(let refusal) = trial,
183	            refusal.reason == FramingWant.noSubjects(clip.id)
184	        else { return call }
185	        let view = scope.flatMap { document.project.scoped($0) } ?? document.project
186	        guard let entry = FramingAnalysis.windows(clips: [clip.id], in: view).first,
187	            let media = view.snapshot.media(entry.media)
188	        else { return call }
189	        if follow == .cursor {
190	            // VR-50 (i): the cursor file in place of the analysis; never a wait.
191	            guard let shown = view.snapshot.clip(clip.id) else { return call }
192	            let files: [UInt32: URL]
193	            do {
194	                files = try AutoZoom.cursorFiles([shown], in: view.snapshot)
195	            } catch {
196	                throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
197	            }
198	            return call.with(
199	                reading: nil,
200	                cursor: CursorReading(media: media, windows: entry.windows, files: files))
201	        }
202	        guard let cacheDir = document.cacheDirectory else {
203	            throw ToolError(message: ProjectDocument.AnalysisRequestError.noCache.localizedDescription)
204	        }
205	        let requests: [AnalysisRequest]
206	        do {
207	            requests = try FramingAnalysis.requests(clips: [clip.id], in: document, project: view)
208	        } catch {
209	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
210	        }
211	        return call.with(
212	            reading: FramingReading(
213	                media: media, windows: entry.windows, cacheDir: cacheDir, requests: requests),
214	            cursor: nil)
215	    }
216	
217	    /// `mics` / `mic_faces` (VR-60 (a)): nil when absent, else whole numbers the core
218	    /// checks itself (an unknown microphone, a 0, a repeat). `make_vertical_version` reads
219	    /// its own two through it (VR-64 (a)).
220	    func numbersArg(_ a: [String: Any], _ key: String) throws -> [UInt32]? {
221	        guard let raw = a[key], !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }
222	        guard let list = raw as? [Any] else {
223	            throw ToolError(message: "\(key) must be a list of whole numbers.")
224	        }
225	        return try list.map { value in
226	            guard let number = value as? NSNumber, CFGetTypeID(number) != CFBooleanGetTypeID(),
227	                let n = Self.whole(number), n >= 0, n <= Int(UInt32.max)
228	            else { throw ToolError(message: "\(key) must be a list of whole numbers.") }
229	            return UInt32(n)
230	        }
231	    }
232	
233	    /// A whole number of pixels for `from_width` / `from_height`, nil when
234	    /// absent; the core refuses a 0 itself.
235	    private func sideArg(_ a: [String: Any], _ key: String) throws -> UInt32? {
236	        guard let value = try intArg(a, key) else { return nil }
237	        guard value >= 0, value <= Int(UInt32.max) else {
238	            throw ToolError(message: "\(key) must be a whole number of pixels, not \(value).")
239	        }
240	        return UInt32(value)
241	    }
242	
243	    /// Wants the requests (non-empty) under an owner of the call's own and
244	    /// waits up to CJ-25's bound: nil once every one landed; past the bound
245	    /// the `analyzing` answer with `note(percent)`, the want held
246	    /// (`FramingWant`); a failure or a Stop throws naming the kind and the
247	    /// media, a Stop saying "so <unmade>.". `reframe_clip`'s and
248	    /// `make_vertical_version`'s wait (spec §11 VR-28, VR-37).
249	    func waitForAnalysis(
250	        _ requests: [AnalysisRequest], document: ProjectDocument, stop: AgentCallCancel?,
251	        unmade: String, note: @escaping (Int) -> String
252	    ) throws -> String? {
253	        let lane = AnalysisLane.shared
254	        let owner = lane.newOwner()
255	        lane.want(
256	            requests, owner: owner,
257	            alive: { document.isOpenForAnalysis && !(stop?.isCancelled ?? false) },
258	            settled: { document.packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk() })
259	        let outcome = lane.wait(
260	            for: requests, owner: owner,
261	            deadline: Date().addingTimeInterval(AnalysisLane.callWaitLimit),
262	            cancelled: { stop?.isCancelled ?? false })
263	        let open = requests.first { lane.run(of: $0)?.outcome != .landed } ?? requests[0]
264	        let named = "The \(open.kind.rawValue) analysis of media \(open.media.id)"
265	        switch outcome {
266	        case .landed:
267	            lane.release(owner: owner)
268	            return nil
269	        case .failed(let why):
270	            lane.release(owner: owner)
271	            throw ToolError(message: "\(named) failed: \(why).")
272	        case .cancelled:
273	            lane.release(owner: owner)
274	            throw ToolError(
275	                message: "\(named) was stopped before it finished, so \(unmade).")
276	        case .timedOut:
277	            let hold = FramingWant(requests: requests)
278	            lane.want(
279	                requests, owner: owner,
280	                alive: { document.isOpenForAnalysis && !hold.done },
281	                settled: {
282	                    hold.settle()
283	                    document.packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()
284	                })
285	            return try onMain {
286	                let covered = FramingWant.covered(requests)
287	                let media = FramingWant.notLanded(requests)
288	                let percent = Int((covered * 100).rounded())
289	                return try self.jsonResult([
290	                    "ok": true,
291	                    "analyzing": ["media": media.map { Int($0) }, "covered": covered],
292	                    "note": note(percent),
293	                    "project": self.summary(document),
294	                ])
295	            }
296	        }
297	    }
298	}
299	
300	/// The want `reframe_clip` leaves held past CJ-25's bound (spec §11 VR-28):
301	/// done once every request has ended, which `settled` marks, so the lane
302	/// drops the owner at its next poll; the owner is never released, so the
303	/// jobs run on after the call has answered. Its own `NSLock`, never the
304	/// lane's: `alive` is asked under the lane's lock.
305	final class FramingWant: @unchecked Sendable {
306	    /// The undo step's name.
307	    static let actionName = "Reframe Clip"
308	
309	    /// VR-26's tenth refusal, the one sentence a trial waits for; built as
310	    /// `core/src/edit_reframe.rs`'s `no_subjects` builds it, and pinned by
311	    /// `core/tests/reframe_clip.rs`.
312	    static func noSubjects(_ clip: UInt32) -> String {
313	        "clip \(clip) has no subjects to follow; analyze it first"
314	    }
315	
316	    private let lock = NSLock()
317	    private var ended = false
318	    private let requests: [AnalysisRequest]
319	
320	    init(requests: [AnalysisRequest]) {
321	        self.requests = requests
322	    }
323	
324	    var done: Bool {
325	        lock.lock()
326	        defer { lock.unlock() }
327	        return ended
328	    }
329	
330	    /// Main thread, from the owner's `settled`: done once every request's
331	    /// run has an outcome.
332	    func settle() {
333	        let lane = AnalysisLane.shared
334	        let all = requests.allSatisfy { lane.run(of: $0)?.outcome != nil }
335	        guard all else { return }
336	        lock.lock()
337	        ended = true
338	        lock.unlock()
339	    }
340	
341	    /// The share of the requests' missing indices their kinds' markers now
342	    /// cover (`AnalysisStore.coveredCount`), rounded to 2 decimals.
343	    static func covered(_ requests: [AnalysisRequest]) -> Double {
344	        var total = 0
345	        var held = 0
346	        for request in requests {
347	            let marker = AnalysisStore.readMarker(
348	                request.kind, media: request.media.id, in: request.cacheDir)
349	            let ranges = marker.map { $0.answers(for: request.stamp) ? $0.ranges : [] } ?? []
350	            for range in request.ranges {
351	                total += range.count
352	                held += AnalysisStore.coveredCount(range, covered: ranges)
353	            }
354	        }
355	        guard total > 0 else { return 1 }
356	        return (Double(held) / Double(total) * 100).rounded() / 100
357	    }
358	
359	    /// The media whose requests have not all landed, in request order.
360	    static func notLanded(_ requests: [AnalysisRequest]) -> [UInt32] {
361	        var media: [UInt32] = []
362	        for request in requests where AnalysisLane.shared.run(of: request)?.outcome != .landed {
363	            if !media.contains(request.media.id) { media.append(request.media.id) }
364	        }
365	        return media
366	    }
367	}
368

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// `switch_layout` (road map "creator-jobs" CO6, spec §11 CO-60…CO-66),
4	/// mirroring Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸ (`switchCameraLayout` in
5	/// `EditorViewController+Layout.swift`, which sends this op at the playhead
6	/// with `duration` and `curve` left to the core): one op, one undo step
7	/// "Camera Layout", every refusal the core's sentence. Since CO7 (spec §11
8	/// CO-70) an omitted or null `focus` is filled from the camera clip's cached
9	/// person masks, as the menu and the Picture sub-tab's Layout section fill
10	/// it, and the answer carries the `focus` sent.
11	extension AgentServer {
12	
13	    /// What the first main-thread hop resolves.
14	    private struct LayoutCall {
15	        let document: ProjectDocument
16	        let camera: UInt32
17	        let screen: UInt32?
18	        let layout: CameraLayoutKind
19	        let shape: CameraLayoutShape?
20	        let corner: CameraLayoutCorner?
21	        let at: Ticks
22	        let duration: Ticks?
23	        let curve: Curve?
24	        let focus: (Double, Double)?
25	        let nest: Bool?
26	        let through: Ticks?
27	        /// The masks to fill `focus` from, when the caller left it out.
28	        let inputs: CameraLayoutFocus.Inputs?
29	        let asked: ReelProject
30	        let scope: UInt32?
31	
32	        func op(focus: (Double, Double)?) -> ReelOp {
33	            .switchLayout(
34	                camera: camera, screen: screen, layout: layout, shape: shape, corner: corner,
35	                at: at, duration: duration, curve: curve, focus: focus, nest: nest,
36	                through: through)
37	        }
38	    }
39	
40	    /// **Runs on the SERVER thread** (`creatorOffMainTools`): one main hop resolves the
41	    /// arguments and the camera's cached masks, the centroid is read here, and a last main hop
42	    /// refuses when the project or the scope changed meanwhile and applies as one undo step.
43	    func switchLayout(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
44	        guard !Thread.isMainThread else {
45	            throw ToolError(
46	                message: "switch_layout must run on the server thread — its name is missing "
47	                    + "from AgentServer.creatorOffMainTools.")
48	        }
49	        let call = try onMain { try self.resolveLayout(a) }
50	        let filled = call.inputs.flatMap { CameraLayoutFocus.focus($0) }
51	        return try onMain {
52	            let document = call.document
53	            guard document.project === call.asked, document.scope == call.scope else {
54	                throw ToolError(
55	                    message: "the project changed while switch_layout read the camera's person "
56	                        + "masks, so nothing was laid out. Call switch_layout again.")
57	            }
58	            var focus = call.focus ?? filled
59	            // A filled focus is in the camera media's pixels: never sent to the nest clip
60	            // that `nest: true` puts in the camera's place (CO-70).
61	            if call.focus == nil, filled != nil, call.nest == true,
62	                let nested = self.addressed([call.op(focus: filled)], document).first,
63	                !CameraLayoutCommand.keepsFocus(
64	                    nested: nested, camera: call.camera, document: document)
65	            {
66	                focus = nil
67	            }
68	            let answer: Any = focus.map { [$0.0, $0.1] } ?? NSNull()
69	            return try self.editResult(
70	                document, CameraLayoutCommand.actionName, [call.op(focus: focus)],
71	                ["focus": answer])
72	        }
73	    }
74	
75	    /// The arguments in the op's order — every required one read before an id is looked up,
76	    /// so a missing one is named as missing whatever the others hold — and the camera's masks
77	    /// when `focus` is left out.
78	    private func resolveLayout(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> LayoutCall {
79	        let document = try target(a)
80	        _ = try idArg(a, "camera")
81	        let layout = try requiredEnumArg(a, "layout", CameraLayoutKind.self)
82	        let at = try timeArg(a, "at", document)
83	        let camera = try clipArg(a, "camera", document)
84	        var screen: UInt32?
85	        if let raw = a["screen"], !(raw is NSNull) {
86	            screen = try clipArg(a, "screen", document).id
87	        }
88	        let focus = try pointArg(a, "focus")
89	        return LayoutCall(
90	            document: document, camera: camera.id, screen: screen, layout: layout,
91	            shape: try enumArg(a, "shape", CameraLayoutShape.self),
92	            corner: try enumArg(a, "corner", CameraLayoutCorner.self), at: at,
93	            duration: try optionalTimeArg(a, "duration", document),
94	            curve: try enumArg(a, "curve", Curve.self), focus: focus,
95	            nest: try boolArg(a, "nest"),
96	            through: try optionalTimeArg(a, "through", document),
97	            inputs: focus == nil ? CameraLayoutFocus.inputs(camera: camera.id, in: document) : nil,
98	            asked: document.project, scope: document.scope)
99	    }
100	
101	    /// Two finite numbers, `[x, y]`, or nil when absent or null.
102	    private func pointArg(_ a: [String: Any], _ key: String) throws -> (Double, Double)? {
103	        guard let raw = a[key], !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }
104	        let numbers = (raw as? [Any])?.compactMap { value -> Double? in
105	            guard let number = value as? NSNumber,
106	                CFGetTypeID(number) != CFBooleanGetTypeID()
107	            else { return nil }
108	            return number.doubleValue
109	        }
110	        guard let numbers, numbers.count == 2, (raw as? [Any])?.count == 2,
111	            numbers.allSatisfy(\.isFinite)
112	        else {
113	            throw ToolError(message: "\(key) must be two numbers, [x, y].")
114	        }
115	        return (numbers[0], numbers[1])
116	    }
117	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`

  callback, `.graphicsDidChange` with sorted names — every module and
  `library: true` when the font/asset set moved; with NO names when the
  folder holds no module and only the library moved, which still posts, G5b).

  `uniqueModuleName(_:)`, the one free-name rule (`-copy`, `-copy-N`)
  Duplicate and Insert ▸ Graphic share, which takes a name as held when the
  scan OR the disk has it (`holdsModule(named:)`, #75); `write(name:source:)`
  and `importFile` land through `land(at:writing:)`, whose `.partial` is
  removed on any failure; and `removeScratchRoot()`, which removes an untitled
  root after `stop()` — from `packageDidMove(to:)` and `stopGraphicStore()`
  (G-19 (d)). It also holds the app's delete and rename, each inside
  `onQueue` (main only, never on the store's queue) so no pass runs between
  their steps: `removeModule(named:)` keeps the file's bytes and then removes
  it, refusing when the text could not be kept, and `moveModule(from:to:)`
  moves the file, journals the pair and reads it back — a rename that cannot
  be journalled is refused — and then moves its history, a throw leaving the
  file and the history where they were and the journal put back as it was
  read (its bytes, or no file: `renameJournalBytes` / `putBackRenameJournal`
  in `GraphicStore+History.swift`), so a refused rename journals no pair; a
  crash between the three steps is G-28 (f)'s limit; neither rescans.

  `noModuleSentence(_:)` the one sentence for an absent module.

  (spec §11 G-27..G-29): `graphics/history/<name>/<%06d sequence>-<revision>.js`,
  the last `historyLimit` (10) per module, and `history/renames.json`, at
  most `renameJournalLimit` (32) pairs. `keepReplaced`, called by `pass` on
  the queue before it stores its scan, keeps the bytes a module's new text
  replaced and drops the new text's own revision, so history never holds the
  current text; nothing is kept at `start()` or for a removal the app did not
  make, and `start()` drops each module's current revision from its history.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.
